why: Canary 1.1 introduces a new 5xx failure mode that stable 1.0 does not have. Evidence from the 120s / 9814-request load test: canary served 2455 requests with 10 5xx (0.41%) while stable served 7359 requests with 0 5xx (0.00%). The errors are not spread out - all 10 land on /checkout, giving canary /checkout a 2.07% error rate (10/483) against 0.00% (0/1455) for stable /checkout. /browse and /search are clean on both versions, so the regression is isolated to the checkout path. Latency is not the problem and gives no cover for the errors: canary p50 28ms vs stable 32ms, p95 96ms vs 94ms, p99 105ms vs 104ms, and per-endpoint latencies match within 1-2ms. The time series shows the errors are persistent rather than a startup blip - canary 5xx counts are 1, 3, 3, 3 across the 0-30s, 30-60s, 60-90s and 90-120s windows (stable 0 in every window), and canary p95 stays flat at 95-97ms throughout, so the pod was warm and still failing. Judgement: a sustained, version-specific failure on the revenue-critical checkout path is exactly the case where a bad promote hurts customers - at 100% traffic this projects to roughly 2% of all checkouts failing. The release blockage from rolling back is recoverable; broken checkouts are not. Rolling back and asking the owning team to reproduce the /checkout 5xx with the canary build before re-attempting.
